fichas.title: Scenery stage
fichas.summary: The classical stage system used a main stage with sliding painted scenery for rapid scene changes. A small rear stage provided space for deeper stage perspectives.
uses: Change scenes by sliding painted scenery
Provide space for deeper stage perspectives

fichas.title: Full stage
fichas.summary: A full stage supplements the main stage with wings and understages, allowing complete scenery sets to be prepared and moved during a performance. The technical arrangement of turntables and lifting elements should be established early.
uses: Prepare and change elaborate scenery during performances
Move scenery using wagons, lifting platforms, or turntables

fichas.title: Proportions and mobile scenery of the stage
fichas.summary: Stage proportions are developed from auditorium sight lines. The stage serves as both an acting area and a handling and working area. Its mobile scenery surface can use adjustable-height platforms or be divided into separate flats.
uses: Adjust scenery surface height and form

fichas.title: Section of stage
fichas.summary: The stage-space size depends on the scenery sets kept ready for rapid movement onto the stage; at least one rear space and one wing are usual. An iron safety curtain must close the fire compartment between auditorium and stage in case of fire, and its space must remain clear of cables and scenery.
uses: Keep scenery sets ready for rapid transfer to the stage
Separate the auditorium and stage fire compartments with a safety curtain

dimensions.label: Safety curtain closure time
dimensions.context: Maximum stated time for closing the fire compartment between auditorium and stage in case of fire.
dimensions.ocr_raw: within 30 s in case of fire.

fichas.title: Stage direction room
fichas.summary: The stage direction room provides control of stage lighting and sound and accommodates sound-mixing, lighting, computer, and projection equipment.
